# isTextStyle

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is a text style.</link-summary>

<web-summary>isTextStyle() — Checks whether a value is a text style. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>appsscript/sheet</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function isTextStyle(value: unknown): value is GoogleAppsScript.Spreadsheet.TextStyle;
```

An Apps Script service object has no constructor a script can test against, so the guard reads the tag the object reports for itself: `value.toString() === "TextStyle"`. A plain object that reports the same tag passes too, which in practice means a test double.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description         |
| :-------- | :-------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `unknown` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is a text style; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `GoogleAppsScript.Spreadsheet.TextStyle` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
const style = SpreadsheetApp.newTextStyle().setBold(true).build();

isTextStyle(style); // => true
isTextStyle({}); // => false
isTextStyle(null); // => false
```
